title: Algebraicity ascends representable morphisms of fibred groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use categories fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, their morphisms, 2-fibre products and scheme-valued objects as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic stacks as in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Let $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of categories fibred in groupoids with $\mathcal Y$ an algebraic stack. Suppose that for each $S$-scheme $T$ and object $T\to\mathcal Y$, the 2-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is naturally equivalent over $T$ to an algebraic space $Z_T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. If, in addition, every $Z_T\to T$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts and $\mathcal Y\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, then $\mathcal X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Here local finite presentation for a stack over a scheme means that a smooth surjective scheme atlas has locally finitely presented composite to that scheme [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No initial stack hypothesis on $\mathcal X$ is needed.

source.place: Tags 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic) and 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic); local finite presentation uses stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06Q2 (definition-locally-finite-presentation) and 06Q3 (lemma-composition-finite-presentation).

proof.text: First check faithfulness and the relative sheaf hypothesis. If $a,b:x\to x'$ have $j(a)=j(b)$ over $T$, then $b^{-1}a$ is an automorphism of $(\mathrm{id}_T,x,1)$ in $h_T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, using $jx:T\to\mathcal Y$. The representing equivalence with the discrete groupoid $Z_T$ forces this automorphism to be the identity, hence $a=b$. For any $y:T\to\mathcal Y$, the presheaf $P_y$ of classes of pairs $(x,\phi:y|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}jx)$ is naturally the presheaf of $Z_T$ on $T$-schemes: these are exactly the objects of the specified 2-fibre product, and its representing equivalence identifies their classes with sections. The identification respects pullback because the equivalence is over $T$. Algebraic spaces are fppf sheaves, hence sheaves for etale coverings, which are particular fppf coverings.

source.place: Tags 05UN and 02ZY (lemma-criterion-map-representable-spaces-fibred-in-groupoids), necessary direction written out

proof.text: The algebraic-stack hypothesis makes $\mathcal Y$ an etale stack. Step 1 gives faithful fibre functors and etale sheaves $P_y$ for every object $y$ over every scheme. Apply faithful relative-sheaf descent to $j$. It gives etale descent for both arrows and objects in $\mathcal X$. In particular $\mathcal X$ is an etale stack without any initial descent assumption.

source.place: Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic), stack assertion, using stacks.tex Tag 0CKJ

proof.text: Check the diagonal on $T\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$, given by $x_1,x_2\in\mathcal X(T)$. Let $B=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(jx_1,jx_2)$ over $T$; it is an algebraic space by the diagonal condition on $\mathcal Y$. Explicitly a diagonal fibre triple $(y,a:y\to jx_1,b:y\to jx_2)$ maps to $ba^{-1}$, with inverse $\alpha\mapsto(jx_1,1,\alpha)$. Let $P(V)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X(V)}(x_1|_V,x_2|_V)$ on $T$-schemes, with $P\to B$ induced by $j$. For a scheme $H\to B$ let $\alpha:jx_1|_H\to jx_2|_H$ be its section. The space $A=H\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ along $jx_1|_H$ has sections $s_1=(x_1|_H,1)$ and $s_2=(x_2|_H,\alpha)$. The equalizer $E$ of these sections is the scheme pullback of the representable diagonal of the algebraic space $A$. Equality of the two sections of $A$ means existence of a unique arrow between their corresponding fibre-product objects. The arrow equation is $j(\beta)=\alpha$. Consequently $H\times_BP\cong h_E$, naturally in all scheme tests. Regard $P$ as a presheaf on $S$-schemes by retaining the map to $T$ in each section. The presheaf-over-space bootstrap, with target $B$, now makes $P$ an algebraic space. The same triple-to-$ba^{-1}$ formula for $\mathcal X$ identifies $P$ with the chosen scheme test of its diagonal. Thus every such test is an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), (1) iff (2), verified on objects; bootstrap.tex Tag 02YS (lemma-representable-by-spaces-over-space) applied to the relative Isom presheaf

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$. By the hypothesis its pullback $A=V\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic space over $V$. The representable smooth calculus for arbitrary fibred groupoids makes $A\to\mathcal X$ representable by algebraic spaces, smooth and surjective, since it is a 2-base change of that atlas. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme chart $U\to A$. The same calculus identifies its properties as a map of fibred groupoids, makes it smooth, and makes the composite $U\to\mathcal X$ representable, smooth and surjective. Together with steps 2 and 3 this meets all three conditions in the definition of algebraic stack.

source.place: Tag 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic), pulled-back atlas, refined by an etale scheme chart; Tags 0302, 045B and 045C

proof.text: Under the additional hypotheses choose the atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$ in step 4 with $V\to S$ locally of finite presentation, as the stated atlas definition of that hypothesis permits. The hypothesis on $Z_T\to T$, applied with $T=V$, says precisely that $U\to A\to V$ is a locally finitely presented scheme map for the etale scheme chart chosen there. Composition of locally finitely presented scheme morphisms therefore makes $U\to V\to S$ locally of finite presentation. The smooth surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ from step 4 with this structural composite witnesses local finite presentation of $\mathcal X\to S$ in the convention of the item.

New node lem-sfb-relative-sheaf-fibred-descent is exactly 0CKJ on (Sch/S)_et, with the orientation of φ inverted, which gives an isomorphic presheaf in groupoids. It is statement-only and self-contained, and it is not a restatement of the item: it is the generic stack half of 05UN, with no representability hypothesis. Small cases agree: over the terminal stack it says setoid fibred categories with a sheaf of classes are stacks; dropping faithfulness or the sheaf hypothesis gives counterexamples; for empty F both sides fail. The rg -L search for 0CKJ/05UN/05UM/05UL and for faithful+descent found no duplicate. lem-sfb-representable-fibred-category-stack only allows scheme fibres and is a special case; lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp is the open-substack special case of the item. Step 1: faithfulness via the automorphism (id_T, b^-1 a) of (id_T, x, 1), killed by the discrete equivalence; P_y is the fibre of Z_T; étale covers are fppf covers directly from def-weil-etale-morphism and def-pc-fppf-site. Step 2: applies the new node. Step 3: with A = H x_Y X and sections s1 = (x1, 1), s2 = (x2, α), an arrow between them is a w with j(w) = α, unique by step 1, so H x_B P = h_E for E the pullback of the diagonal of A; the bootstrap node (02YS, no sheaf hypothesis on P) then applies with target B over all scheme tests. Step 4: pulled-back atlas and étale chart through the calculus clauses (base change, étale implies smooth, chart comparison, composition), meeting all three clauses of def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack. Step 5: existential atlas convention, chart lfp hypothesis and the 01TR Mathlib composition give U -> S lfp. No cycle; no SGA. The tool_uses entry (presheaf bootstrap, same unit) is accepted. Batch-5: the closure reaches no thm-/cor- node of trf/pd and no nt- or trace-transport node, only definitions and foundational space/projective-bundle units (sk-i-curve-zero, sk-i-additivity, sk-lem-finite). lean.statement: theorem isAlgebraicModuliStack_of_representable {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)} {Y : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)} (j : BasedFunctor X Y) (hX : IsFibredInGroupoids X) (hY : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y) (hj : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces j) : IsAlgebraicModuliStack X ∧ ((∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) Y), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange j T t Z p ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Z.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale b → LocallyOfFinitePresentation ((yoneda.preimage (b ≫ p)).left)) → (∃ (V : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj V)) Y), IsSmoothModuliAtlas Y V a ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation V.hom) → ∃ (U : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) X), IsSmoothModuliAtlas X U a ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation U.hom)
lean.note: Both clauses in one conjunction; source initially only fibred in groupoids. The conditional local finite presentation clause uses projection-compatible space presentations, all etale scheme charts, and the accepted existential smooth-atlas convention. Independent object and morphism universes for source and target.
